dossier.public_summary: The dip is only ~6 ppm in one sector and deep in two others, changing by more than a factor of ten between sectors from the same pipeline, so it does not behave like a planet transit. Together with a weak and inconsistent signal this favours noise or stellar variability over a true transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by >150% between sectors, far beyond measurement errors. A planet must be achromatic/steady within a pipeline, so this favours variability or a few bad/no transits over a transiting planet.
reasons.value: p_constant=1.353e-22 depth_change_pct=151.9 per_sector: 18=10591 ppm, 58=167 ppm, 85=11375 ppm

reasons.why: The change is within a single source (TESS-SPOC), so it is not a product/calibration offset. One sector shows no detection at all, the other a deep dip, inconsistent with a planet.

reasons.why: SNR is near the threshold and signal is dominated by a few events (share 0.3827) with early ingress and disparate durations, suggesting the detection is driven by outliers/variability rather than a repeatable flat-bottom (v_sigma=-2.875) transit.
